nodes.name: VG Ar-0 Synthesis
nodes.procedure: Carbon fiber paper (CFP; Toray 090) was inserted into the plasma chamber which was evacuated to < 2 × 10⁻² Pa. Ar flowing at 10 sccm was introduced and the pressure was adjusted to 1.5 Pa. The radio-frequency induced plasma was ignited at 13.56 MHz with a power of 1000 W to pretreat the CFP, improving VG adhesion on the substrate. After 10 min, CH₄ and H₂ were introduced at 10 sccm each to initiate the VG growth for 10 min, forming pristine VG (VG Ar-0).
nodes.source_text: Synthesis of VG Ar-0 and VG Ar-5: The VG Ar-0 and VG Ar-5 supports were synthesized via a plasma-enhanced chemical vapor deposition (PECVD) method...

nodes.name: VG Ar-5 Edge-Rich Treatment
nodes.procedure: To produce the edge rich VG (VG Ar-5), the precursor gasses were removed from the chamber by pumping it down to < 5 × 10⁻³ Pa. Ar was then reintroduced at a flow rate of 10 sccm, and the pressure increased to 1.5 Pa. The Ar plasma was then reignited and sustained for 5 min to induce branching, creating the edge rich graphene.
nodes.source_text: To produce the edge rich VG (VG Ar-5), the precursor gasses were removed... Ar plasma was then reignited and sustained for 5 min...

nodes.name: Pt/VG Ar-0 Impregnation & Reduction
nodes.procedure: 1 μg cm⁻² of equivalent Pt loading was added dropwise to the VG Ar-0 supports using a 200 ppm H₂PtCl₆ precursor solution and left to impregnate for 1 h at room temperature. Then, excess precursor was removed by dipping the electrode in deionized water, and the substrate was dried under a stream of nitrogen. The catalysts were then reduced at 200°C in a H₂ stream (20% H₂, balance Ar at 50 mL min⁻¹) for 1 h, with a ramping rate of 5°C min⁻¹.

The catalysts were then reduced at 200°C in a H₂ stream (20% H₂, balance Ar at 50 mL min⁻¹) for 1 h, with a ramping rate of 5°C min⁻¹.

nodes.name: Pt/C Ink Preparation & Drop Casting
nodes.procedure: An ink consisting of 0.6 mg of 20 wt% Pt/C (Sigma-Aldrich), 3000 μL deionized H₂O, 2925 μL ethanol, and 75 μL Nafion solution (resulting in a Pt/C concentration of 0.1 g L⁻¹) was ultrasonicated for at least 20 min, and then 12.5 μL was drop casted onto 0.25 cm² of graphite paper (Graphene-Paper, Sigma-Aldrich) and dried at room temperature, resulting in a total Pt loading of 1 μg cm⁻².
nodes.source_text: The commercial Pt/C sample (denoted as 1 μg Pt/C) was prepared by creating an ink consisting of 0.6 mg of 20 wt% Pt/C...

nodes.characterization_summary: HAADF-STEM images show high contrast dispersed Pt single atoms primarily anchored on graphene edges (terraces/step edges) in Pt/VG Ar-5, with some on basal planes in Pt/VG Ar-0.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Figure 2c shows a high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (HAADF-STEM) image of Pt/VG Ar-5 where high contrast dispersed Pt single atoms can be observed.

nodes.characterization_summary: ICP-MS measurements found Pt loading of 0.76 μg cm⁻² for Pt/VG Ar-0 and 0.71 μg cm⁻² for Pt/VG Ar-5 based on nominal loading of 1 μg cm⁻².
nodes.evidence_snippet: Inductively coupled plasma mass spectrometry (ICP-MS) measurements found that the Pt loading was 0.76 and 0.71 μg cm⁻² for Pt/VG Ar-0 and Pt/VG Ar-5, respectively...

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt LIII-edge XANES shows higher white line intensity for both catalysts vs Pt foil (non-metallic Pt with unoccupied 5d states), Pt/VG Ar-5 lower than Pt/VG Ar-0 indicating higher 5d electron population and lower oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The higher white line intensity of the Pt LIII-edge of Pt/VG Ar-0 and Pt/VG Ar-5 compared to Pt foil indicate that Pt is in a non-metallic form with unoccupied density in valence shells. Between Pt/VG Ar-5 and Pt/VG Ar-0, a lower white line intensity is shown for Pt/VG Ar-5, indicating a higher electron population in the 5d orbitals and a lower oxidation state.

nodes.characterization_summary: Pt 4f XPS shows peaks at 73.0 eV (4f7/2) and 76.1 eV (4f5/2) for Pt/VG Ar-5 vs 73.1 eV and 76.3 eV for Pt/VG Ar-0, indicating higher electron population in Pt/VG Ar-5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: A peak located at 73.0 eV (4f7/2) with the corresponding spin-orbit split peak at 76.1 eV (4f5/2) was observed for Pt/VG Ar-5, while these peaks shifted to 73.1 eV (4f7/2) and 76.3 eV (4f5/2) respectively, for Pt/VG Ar-0.

nodes.characterization_summary: FT-EXAFS shows single coordination peak at ≈1.7 Å (Pt-O or Pt-C) confirming atomic dispersion; coordination number 5.00 for Pt/VG Ar-0 vs 3.58 for Pt/VG Ar-5; WT confirms mixture of Pt-O and Pt-C coordination.
nodes.evidence_snippet: For Pt/VG Ar-0 and Pt/VG Ar-5, a single coordination at ≈1.7 Å can be found, corresponding to either Pt-O or Pt-C bonding, confirming the atomic dispersion of Pt on both supports. The Pt/VG Ar-0 sample exhibited a higher coordination number for the Pt-O or Pt-C bond of 5.00 on average, compared to 3.58 for Pt/VG Ar-5.

nodes.characterization_summary: XRD shows no bulk crystalline Pt phases, only graphitic (002), (100), (101), (004) peaks from VG support.
nodes.evidence_snippet: X-ray diffraction (XRD) was undertaken on Pt/VG Ar-0 and Pt/VG Ar-5, and demonstrated no bulk crystalline Pt phases, with peaks only corresponding to the (002), (100), (101), and (004) graphitic diffraction peaks...

nodes.characterization_summary: Raman ID/IG ratio 1.9 for Pt/VG Ar-5 vs 1.3 for Pt/VG Ar-0 due to increased Raman-active edge density; minimal change after Pt deposition.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The ratio of intensity of the D and G peaks (ID/IG) demonstrates the degree of disorder in the graphene. As expected, VG Ar-5 had a significantly larger ID/IG ratio (1.9) compared to that of VG Ar-0 (1.3)...

nodes.characterization_summary: Angle-dependent C K-edge NEXAFS shows dampened π* peak intensity increase after Pt deposition, more pronounced for Pt/VG Ar-5 indicating stronger π-electron interaction at edges.
nodes.evidence_snippet: By comparing the partial electron yield (PEY) before and after Pt deposition, changes to the C 1s to π* peak are indicative of the Pt electronic states that may be coordinated through oxygen-containing bridges interacting with π-electrons of the graphene edges.

nodes.characterization_summary: Double layer capacitance Cdl = 5.22 mF cm⁻² for Pt/VG Ar-0 and 12.6 mF cm⁻² for Pt/VG Ar-5 (2.4× increase); HUPD CV shows more pronounced H adsorption/desorption peaks for Pt/VG Ar-5.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Cdl for Pt/VG Ar-0 was measured and calculated to be 5.22 mF cm⁻², while for Pt/VG Ar-5 this was 12.6 mF cm⁻², indicative of a 2.4-time increase in ECSA... CV curves were undertaken... to investigate hydrogen underpotential deposition (HUPD) characteristics... Pt/VG Ar-5 had more pronounced hydrogen adsorption/desorption peaks compared to Pt/VG Ar-0.

nodes.characterization_summary: EIS at η=30 mV shows charge transfer resistance R3 = 209 Ω for Pt/VG Ar-0 vs 144 Ω for Pt/VG Ar-5, indicating improved electron transfer for edge-anchored Pt.
nodes.evidence_snippet: EIS... showed a significantly reduced charge transfer resistance (R3 in our simulated circuit...) for Pt/VG Ar-5 over Pt/VG Ar-0 (144 vs 209 Ω) indicative of improved electron transfer kinetics...
